target: AArch64 QEMU virt with PCI VirtIO sound and WAV backend
command: QEMU_VIRT='-machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -m 1024 -device ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -audiodev wav,id=sound0,path=/tmp/zeal-ascii-organ.wav -device virtio-sound-pci,audiodev=sound0' python3 scripts/check-compat.py --probe-demo-ascii-organ
checks: ASCIIOrgan displayed its character table and sound-key prompt.
The injected 'a' key generated a note through the stock Sound(ch - CH_ESC) call.

The QEMU WAV backend captured 17,640 stereo frames at 44.1 kHz (0.4 s); channels matched, peak amplitude was 7,000, and sign transitions measured about 786 Hz, matching the requested note after resampling.
Shift-Escape returned to the graphical terminal, 40+2 evaluated to 42, and zstatus reported failed=0.
scope_note: This supersedes the keyboard-only partial result in demo-ascii-organ-qemu-2026-11-03.json for QEMU VirtIO sound. It does not verify audible host output in live UTM or Raspberry Pi hardware.
